title: Derived closed-pushforward models have the expected open-site stalk homology
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $x\in Z$, and $U\subseteq Y$ an open neighbourhood of $i(x)$. Let $K$ be any cochain complex indexed by $\mathbb Z$ of module sheaves on the slice site over $U$. Suppose its derived localization $Q(K)$ [def-pc-derived-category] is isomorphic to the restriction of $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)[0]$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply the explicit functor $S_{U,i(x)}$ [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor] degreewise to form $L$. Then $H^0(L)$ is isomorphic as an $\mathcal O_{Y,i(x)}$-module to $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ with scalar action through $i^\sharp_x$, and $H^j(L)=0$ for every $j\ne0$. No projectivity or boundedness of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Sheaves Tag 00AE, Modules Tag 01AG; stalk-model plan steps 3 and 4

proof.text: Apply the exact stalk functor on derived categories to the specified isomorphism e. Use mapDerivedCategoryFactors and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor for restriction and for the stalk functor to identify Q(L) with the single object of the stalk of the restricted pushforward.

Apply nonempty_restriction_stalk_extension_iso to the single complex of the pushforward sheaf and evaluate its isomorphism in degree zero. Restrict scalars along the open immersion's stalk map. This ring map is an isomorphism, hence restriction of scalars is an equivalence and the extension/restriction adjunction unit is invertible. Compose the inverse of the scalar-restricted degree-zero comparison with the inverse unit, and compose with the stalk image of overFunctorEquiv U. This identifies the coefficient module with the original pushforward stalk, without constructing a natural comparison or repeating any germ-linearity proof.

The closed-pushforward stalk theorem gives a bijective additive germ map linear through i.stalkMap x. Regard it as a linear map into the scalar-restricted source unit stalk and use LinearEquiv.ofBijective to form its module isomorphism. Compose with the source-unit stalk isomorphism. Extract the unit-stalk isomorphism from Scheme.ideal_module_product_stalk applied to the identity inclusion of the unit sheaf and the unit coefficient sheaf.

Apply homologyFunctorFactors and the homology functor to the derived isomorphism. At zero use singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso; away from zero use isZero_single_obj_homology. Compose the coefficient isomorphisms at degree zero and transport the vanishing at other degrees.

lean.statement:
theorem openModuleStalk_closedPushforward_homology
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (x : Z) (U : Y.Opens) (hx : i x ∈ U)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (e : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) :
    let L := ((openModuleStalkFunctor Y U ⟨i x, hx⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K
    Nonempty (L.homology 0 ≅
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (i.stalkMap x).hom).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (Z.presheaf.stalk x) (Z.presheaf.stalk x)))) ∧
      (∀ j : ℤ, j ≠ 0 → IsZero (L.homology j))
